channel.title: Devin Desaulniers' Greater Vancouver Real Estate Blog
channel.description: Greater Vancouver and Tri-Cities, BC real estate news, explained in plain language by Devin Desaulniers, Real Estate Associate with Axford Real Estate.

item.title: Port Coquitlam may pause new multiplex applications
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Port Coquitlam council meets tonight with a recommendation to pause new applications that rely on the province's multiplex rules. Nothing has been voted on yet. What that could mean in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Is Port Moody a good place to live?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Is Port Moody a good place to live? The draw is the inlet, trails and SkyTrain in a smaller city in the Tri-Cities, BC. The trade-offs are steep hills, a small purpose-built rental stock and a zone 3 commute.

item.title: Gas is coming down. Vancouver still pays near the top
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: On November 18, Kalibrate put regular gas in Vancouver at 183.7¢/L, second to Victoria at 186.3¢. A 60 L tank still costs about $39 more than in Edmonton. What that means if you're moving to the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: What is winter in the Tri-Cities, BC like?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Winter in the Tri-Cities, BC is mild and wet. Port Moody Glenayre’s 1971–2000 normals put a typical January day at 3.0°C, with 1,955.3 mm of precipitation a year, mostly rain. A newcomer checklist for tires, sidewalks, damp and outages.

item.title: Your mortgage rate hold has an expiry date
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Your mortgage rate hold expires, like the milk in the fridge. The Bank of Canada hiked to 2.50% on Oct. 28. A further 0.25 point rise is a scenario, not a forecast. Figures as of Nov. 18, 2026.

item.title: Vancouver's housing-start trend rose 2% in October
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: CMHC's October 2026 report shows the Vancouver housing-start trend up 2% from September, to 26,586, while B.C.'s trend fell 3%. Actual October starts jumped on multi-unit homes, but the year-to-date total is only 1% above 2025. What that means in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Living near Lafarge Lake–⁠Douglas Station in Coquitlam: a newcomer's guide
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Living near Lafarge Lake–Douglas Station puts Town Centre Park, City Hall and the pool at the Coquitlam end of the Millennium Line. The train to Commercial–Broadway is 35 minutes, before a transfer downtown.

item.title: Vancouver real estate in 2026: strangers are buying houses together
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Two Vancouver families who'd never met teamed up on a $1.85M house, with their own suites and kitchens and a shared basement, yard and freezer. Here's why I like the idea, and what I'd tell any client thinking about co-owning.

item.title: Moving to BC from overseas: first steps in the Tri-Cities, BC
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Moving to BC from overseas? Your first steps in the Tri-Cities, BC: arrange private health insurance for the MSP wait, list your belongings for the border, get a SIN, open a bank account, switch your licence within 90 days, and know BC's half-month deposit limit.

item.title: SD43 school registration for newcomers to the Tri-Cities, BC
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: SD43 school registration for newcomers: most families register at their catchment school with three proofs of a BC address, plus guardianship and ID papers. A long-term lease counts as the main address document, so housing comes first.

item.title: Coquitlam rents buck the Metro Vancouver trend in November
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: liv.rent's November 2026 report shows Metro Vancouver one-bedroom asking rents down 3.2% from a year ago, but Coquitlam is one of only two cities above last year, with two- and three-bedroom rents jumping about 6% in a month. Here's what that means if you're renting or moving to the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Selling a townhouse in Coquitlam: what should you know?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Selling a townhouse in Coquitlam right now means pricing against a benchmark of $962,600, down 6.6% from a year ago, and having your strata paperwork ready before buyers ask. Here's what the latest numbers show and how I'd prepare.

item.title: Living near Moody Centre Station in Port Moody: a newcomer's guide
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Thinking about living near Moody Centre Station in Port Moody? Rocky Point Park is about a 10-minute walk and the St. Johns Street shops about 8, with SkyTrain and the West Coast Express at the same station. Here's what newcomers should know.

item.title: Port Moody eases 2027 energy rules for 2,474 homes in the pipeline
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Port Moody council voted to let 20 projects already in the works skip the next step of the BC Energy Step Code in 2027. Here's what that could mean for presale and new-home buyers and renters in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Moving from Ontario to BC: what changes when you land in the Tri-Cities, BC
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Moving from Ontario to BC? Here's what changes when you settle in the Tri-Cities, BC: OHIP vs the MSP wait, your ICBC licence and vehicle deadlines, 5% GST + 7% PST instead of 13% HST, and BC's half-month deposit limit.

item.title: Where can newcomers find settlement services in the Tri-Cities, BC?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Free settlement services in the Tri-Cities, BC are run by S.U.C.C.E.S.S. and ISSofBC in Coquitlam. Which program you can use depends on your status: federal services for permanent residents, the BC Newcomer Services Program for workers, students and new citizens.

item.title: Buying a presale condo in Port Moody or Coquitlam: what should you know?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Buying a presale condo in Port Moody or Coquitlam means signing for a home that isn't built yet, with your deposit held in trust and a seven-day right to cancel after you get the disclosure statement. Here is what B.C.'s rules cover, the risks to weigh, and the questions I'd ask first.

item.title: Where Canadians are moving: B.C. and Alberta almost an even trade
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: From April to June 2026, Alberta gained 5,893 people from the rest of Canada and B.C. was 2nd at 2,756, while Ontario lost 7,063. Here's the interprovincial migration map, and what it means if you're moving to Greater Vancouver.

item.title: Temporary housing in the Tri-Cities, BC: where to stay while you search
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Need temporary housing in the Tri-Cities, BC while you look for a rental? In Port Moody, Coquitlam and Port Coquitlam, most legal short-term rentals are rooms in the host's own home, so plan your stay early. Here's what newcomers should know about the rules, registration numbers and keeping the stay short.

item.title: Builders and REALTORS® ask B.C.'s new government to rethink housing rules
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Developers and the BC Real Estate Association want the incoming government to review the Step Code, the planned PST expansion and housing taxes, as Metro Vancouver condo construction sits at a 15-year low. My take for buyers, sellers and renters in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: How do you find a family doctor in the Tri-Cities, BC?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: To find a family doctor in the Tri-Cities, BC, register for the province's Health Connect Registry once you have your Personal Health Number. While you wait, urgent and primary care centres in Port Moody and Port Coquitlam, pharmacists and 8-1-1 can help.

item.title: Living near Inlet Centre Station in Port Moody: a newcomer's guide
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Thinking about living near Inlet Centre Station in Port Moody? Suter Brook Village is about a 5-minute walk, City Hall and the library about 10, and the Recreation Complex about 12. Here's what newcomers should know about the area, buses and day-to-day life.

item.title: Canada's foreign buyer ban is staying, with a twist
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Budget 2026 proposes extending Canada's ban on foreign purchases of existing homes to January 1, 2029, while exempting new residential properties. Here's what that means in plain English for Greater Vancouver and the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Renting a basement suite in the Tri-Cities, BC: what should you check?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Renting a basement suite in the Tri-Cities, BC? Check that the suite is self-contained (sharing a kitchen or bathroom with the owner can leave you outside BC's tenancy law), that the utility split is in writing, and that basic safety features are in place. Here's a newcomer checklist.

item.title: BCREA forecast: Greater Vancouver sales seen rising 8.7% in 2027
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: The BC Real Estate Association's new forecast expects Greater Vancouver home sales to slip 3% in 2026, then rise 8.7% in 2027, with average prices down 1.4% this year. My take for buyers, sellers and newcomers in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Where could Canada's population grow most by 2050?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Statistics Canada's medium-growth scenario has Canada adding about 7.03 million people by 2050. Alberta grows fastest (+43.6%), Ontario adds the most people, and B.C. adds 892,700 (+15.7%). Here's what that backdrop means for the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Moving to Greater Vancouver? Your first-week checklist
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Just arrived in Greater Vancouver or the Tri-Cities, BC? A plain day-by-day first-week checklist: MSP, ICBC, BC Hydro and FortisBC, Canada Post forwarding, a Compass Card, SD43 school registration and a doctor.

item.title: Moving from the US to BC: a newcomer's guide to the Tri-Cities, BC
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Moving from the US to BC and settling in Coquitlam, Port Moody or Port Coquitlam? Here's what to sort out: health coverage during the MSP wait, your customs list, importing your car, swapping your licence, and renting from a distance.

item.title: Day 1 to Day 7 in Greater Vancouver: the short checklist from TikTok
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Moving to Greater Vancouver? A short Day 1 to Day 7 checklist from my TikTok: MSP, ICBC, BC Hydro, tenant insurance, Compass Card, school, a family doctor, then a real rain jacket.

item.title: Coquitlam vs Port Moody vs Port Coquitlam: pick your personality
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Coquitlam, Port Moody or Port Coquitlam? A short Tri-Cities, BC personality guide for newcomers choosing between fleece-and-dog energy, high-rise living, or a truck-and-neighbours vibe.
